::: {.lead}
The managers of Byte Bay have money for one new platform, and everyone in
the team has an opinion. Opinions are not enough. Today there are no new
ideas: you use what Lecture 12 taught to check which settings run well on
four PCs, to compare three platforms for one game with three criteria, and
to write a recommendation with a port plan. Do each activity alone. The
results of the activities are at the end of this worksheet: try first,
then compare.
:::

## Recall

- A console has **fixed hardware** (dev kit, certification); a gaming PC
  has **varied hardware** (graphics settings, minimum and recommended
  requirements).
- Cloud gaming: total delay = ping + about 40 ms; racing needs under about
  80 ms.
- A cross-platform game still needs **porting**; **cross-save** keeps one
  progress.
- A comparison: three criteria chosen first, scores from 1 to 5 with
  reasons, totals.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the colour of the box|a bigger screen"}
Why does a PC game need graphics settings?
:   PC players have very different hardware

    Why: Each player chooses the setting that runs well on the PC.

What does a console studio need before release?
:   certification

    Why: The console maker checks the game before it goes on sale.

Which feature lets a player continue on a new platform with one account?
:   cross-save

    Why: Cross-save shares the progress between platforms.
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Will it run well? Specs and settings

The PC version of *Pocket Quest* must run on very different PCs. The **GPU**
and the **memory** decide how fast each frame is drawn:

- a higher setting costs more GPU work per frame: on a weak GPU the frame
  rate falls;
- if the memory is too small for a setting, the game stutters;
- the weakest part is the **bottleneck**;
- the **minimum** requirements come from the weakest supported PC (low
  settings); the **recommended** ones from high settings.

![Pocket Quest: targets per platform (example values).](images/targets.png){width=90%}

{{< sim file="sims/spec-compare.html" poster="sims/spec-compare.png" title="Spec Check: will Pocket Quest run well?" height="700" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Testing only on the team's strong PCs gives wrong requirements: test the
minimum on the weakest supported PC.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Four PCs · 12 min"}
1. In **Spec Check**, find the highest setting that runs at 60 fps or more
   on each of the four devices.
2. Write the minimum and the recommended requirements in your own words.

*Your product:* a table of four devices and two requirement lines.

::: {.check}
| device | best setting at 60 fps or more |
|---|---|
| old laptop (GPU 2, 4 GB) | low: 80 fps |
| office PC (GPU 4, 8 GB) | medium: 80 fps (high gives only 40) |
| handheld PC (GPU 6, 16 GB) | high: 60 fps |
| gaming PC (GPU 12, 16 GB) | ultra: 72 fps |

Minimum: a GPU of 2 points and 4 GB of RAM, for low at 60 fps.
Recommended: a GPU of 6 points and 8 GB of RAM, for high at 60 fps.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Specs"}
Use Spec Check (example points). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="ultra|4K"}
The best 60 fps setting on the old laptop?
:   low

    Why: Medium needs 6 GB of RAM; the laptop has 4 GB.

The frame rate of the office PC on high?
:   40 fps

    Why: High needs 6 points for 60 fps; the office PC has 4.

The bottleneck of the office PC on high?
:   the GPU

    Why: Its 8 GB of RAM are enough; the GPU is too weak.

Which device runs ultra at 60 fps or more?
:   the gaming PC

    Why: 12 points are more than the 10 that ultra needs.
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Three criteria for Star Garden

The two friends of *Star Garden*, a calm puzzle game with short sessions
and no live matches, want **one** new platform: PC, console or cloud
gaming. They have one Windows laptop and little money. Most of their
players use phones or PCs.

- Choose three criteria first: **reach**, **fit for the game**, **cost and
  time**.
- Score each platform from 1 to 5 (5 = best), with a reason for each score.
- Add up; if two totals are close, say which criterion decides.

![A comparison table with three criteria (the Pocket Quest example).](images/platform-table.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · The table for Star Garden · 12 min"}
Make the table for *Star Garden*: three criteria, three platforms, a score
with a reason in every cell, and the totals.

*Your product:* a table with scores, reasons and totals.

::: {.check}
A good table looks like:

| criterion | PC | console | cloud |
|---|---|---|---|
| reach | 4: many players have a PC | 2: few of its players have a console | 2: few use cloud gaming |
| fit for the game | 4: a mouse works well for a puzzle | 3: a controller is slower | 5: the delay does not matter |
| cost and time | 5: the laptop builds it, open store | 1: dev kit and certification | 3: a cloud partner is needed |
| total | **13** | 6 | 10 |

Your scores may differ by one point; what matters is a reason in every
cell. The PC wins clearly; cloud gaming comes second.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The table"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the console|the favourite of the team"}
Why does the console get 1 for cost and time?
:   a dev kit and certification cost money and time

    Why: Console studios need both before release.

Why does cloud gaming fit Star Garden well?
:   a calm puzzle game does not mind the delay

    Why: The delay of the stream matters only for fast games.

PC 13, cloud 10. Which platform comes first?
:   the PC

    Why: It has the highest total.
:::
:::

## Activity 3 · A recommendation with a port plan

The friends want a short recommendation with a plan for the port:

- **what** to do, **why** (two facts from the table) and **what would
  change it**;
- the **port plan**: controls, menus, graphics settings, accounts and
  saves, store rules, testing on the weakest device.

![What changes in a port?](images/port-checklist.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A recommendation without the port plan hides the biggest cost: list the
work before the decision.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 3 · Advice and plan · 10 min"}
Write three sentences of advice for *Star Garden* and a port plan of five
points.

*Your product:* the advice and the plan.

::: {.check}
A good answer looks like: "Port Star Garden to the PC first. The laptop
already builds it and the PC store is open, and many of our players have a
PC. Cloud gaming comes next if a partner offers it." Port plan: 1. mouse
and keyboard; 2. menus for a bigger screen; 3. low, medium and high
settings; 4. cross-save with the same account; 5. minimum and recommended
requirements on the store page, tested on an old laptop.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Advice and port"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a bigger logo|cross-play"}
What must the PC store page show about hardware?
:   minimum and recommended requirements

    Why: Players check whether their PC is strong enough.

A player continues the phone garden on the PC. Which feature?
:   cross-save with one account

    Why: One progress for all platforms.

On which PC do you test the minimum requirements?
:   the weakest supported PC

    Why: The minimum must run there at 60 fps.
:::
:::

## Case study: Port Planner

The first test builds of *Pocket Quest* bring six reports: 20 fps on an old
laptop with the only setting; a console menu that says "Tap to start"; a
certification report about an unplugged controller; a PC store page without
hardware requirements; a player who starts the PC version at level 1 after
level 12 on the phone; and cloud players at 70 ms ping who feel the car
react late. The Game challenge of the interactive page uses these reports.
In the mini-game below you choose the best fix for each one.

{{< sim file="sims/port-planner.html" poster="sims/port-planner.png" title="Port Planner: fix the test reports" kind="game" height="480" >}}

## Exercises

1. What is a bottleneck?
2. The office PC has 8 GB of RAM and a GPU of 4 points. Why does it give
   only 40 fps on high?
3. From which PC do the minimum requirements come?
4. Name three criteria for comparing platforms.
5. Why does every score in a comparison table need a reason?
6. Name four points of a port plan.
7. What does a good recommendation say?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. The weakest part of a device for a task.
2. High needs a GPU of about 6 points for 60 fps; the GPU is the
   bottleneck.
3. From the weakest supported PC, on low settings.
4. For example reach, fit for the game, cost and time.
5. A score is an estimate; the reason shows where it comes from.
6. For example controls, menus, graphics settings, cross-save, store page,
   testing on the weakest device.
7. What to do, why (facts from the table) and what would change it.
:::
